title: Geometry - Lesson 8 Assessment: Composite Perimeter
description: Demonstrate mastery of perimeter problems with missing side lengths in composite figures.

questions.question: Which routine is best for finding the perimeter of a composite rectilinear figure?
options: Find areas, then add square units
Trace the outside boundary, find missing sides, then add outer side lengths
Add only the sides with labels
questions.explanation: Composite perimeter depends on the outside boundary. Missing side lengths must be found before all outer sides are added.

questions.question: A composite figure has outside sides of 12 m, 5 m, 4 m, 3 m, 8 m, and 8 m. What is the perimeter? Enter just the number.
The full width of a step-shaped figure is 18 cm. One horizontal part is 11 cm. What is the other horizontal part that completes the width? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The two horizontal parts across the width must total 18 cm, so 18 - 11 = 7 cm.

questions.question: A side inside a composite figure should be included in the perimeter if it helps split the figure into rectangles.
questions.explanation: Perimeter includes only the outside boundary, not interior dividing lines.

questions.question: Which unit is appropriate for the perimeter of a garden path?
questions.explanation: Perimeter is a distance, so it uses linear units such as meters.

questions.question: An L-shape has outside sides 14 cm, 6 cm, 5 cm, 4 cm, 9 cm, and 10 cm. What is the perimeter? Enter just the number.
A rectilinear figure has total height 16 m. The vertical drop is split into 9 m and a missing vertical side. What is the missing vertical side? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: The vertical parts must total the full height: 16 - 9 = 7 m.

questions.question: A student finds perimeter by adding every number shown, including one interior segment. Explain why the answer is too large.
questions.correctAnswer: The interior segment is not part of the outside boundary. Adding it counts extra distance, so the perimeter becomes too large.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that perimeter measures only the outside boundary.

questions.question: A step-shaped patio has outside sides 20 m, 6 m, 8 m, 5 m, 12 m, and 11 m. What is the perimeter? Enter just the number.
questions.explanation: Add each outside side once: 20 + 6 + 8 + 5 + 12 + 11 = 62 m.

questions.question: Describe the steps you would use to solve a missing-side perimeter problem for a composite figure.
questions.correctAnswer: Trace the outside boundary, label every outer side, use total horizontal or vertical distances to find missing sides, add all outside lengths once, and write linear units.
questions.explanation: A complete method includes boundary tracing, finding missing sides, adding outer sides, and using linear units.
